value.title: Cross-model review r1 — statusline-generation-badge
value.note:
SUBJECT: branch 129-statusline-generation-badge at fc01d0e6, reviewed against origin/main (origin/main is an ancestor of HEAD; the 3-dot diff is the whole delivery: 24 files, +2257/-27).

METHOD: receipts in assets/live-statusline.md were treated as claims, not evidence. I re-ran shellcheck, `cargo test -p pij-harnesses statusline_`, both vitest files, the branch `doctor claude-statusline` verb, and my own timing loop; I read the script, the installer, and every test body rather than the receipt prose. Where the receipts and I agree, I say so and name what I ran. Where I could not independently reproduce (the live omp footer), I label the claim by what I actually checked rather than borrowing the receipt's confidence.

VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES. One HIGH finding falsifies AC1 for exactly the population AC1 was written for, and I reproduced it live on a real dual-present pane. Three further findings are MEDIUM/LOW. Nothing here is a correctness defect in the installer or in u2; the installer and the omp badge are good work and I could not break them.

AC VERDICTS
- AC1 dual-present panes show the rs id with a yellow rs tag — FALSE. See #findings/f1. A real dual-present pane (%3060, pid 87487 in BOTH stores) renders `legacy ⛓ pij-quarrelsome-caribou`, not `rs ⛓ pij-relative-cheetah`, whenever the Claude process env carries a PIJ_SESSION_ID that rs disagrees with — which is the defining condition of the mapped-pair seats this AC targets.
- AC2 legacy-only and unregistered panes render honestly — TRUE, independently reproduced. rs-miss → `legacy ⛓ <legacy id>`; a pane in neither store with no pij binaries on PATH → no pij segment, every other segment intact, exit 0.
- AC3 omp footer names the generation — TRUE by code and unit test on BOTH generations and BOTH surfaces (native `rs·<id>` / `legacy·<id>`, plus the keyed status row with ANSI 33 / ANSI 2). CONFIDENCE NOTE, per claim: I did not start a real omp, so the live-footer half rests on the author's capture; the code-and-test half I verified myself (17/17 index.test.ts, 8/8 session-name.test.ts, watched).
- AC4 rs-first resolution is cheap — FALSE AS WRITTEN, TRUE against the bar prime actually ruled. See #findings/f2. plan.dd.md still says "≤ 50ms over 10 runs"; the author's median is 92.10ms and mine is 67.98ms. Both clear the ruled ≤100ms; neither clears the written 50ms.
- AC5 installer is additive, idempotent, and refuses malformed input — TRUE. 4/4 statusline_ tests watched green; `doctor claude-statusline` reports `installed` for both real homes; and the backup mechanism is confirmed on the operator's real disk, not just in a fixture — `~/.claude/statusline-context.sh.bak-1788315355478` and `.bak-1788316617931` exist beside the original, from both the tilde form and the absolute form of the prior command.

COMPOSITION SEAMS (done-bar d2), examined explicitly:
- u1↔u2 share no file and no symbol. The only seam is the vocabulary: the shell renders `rs`/`legacy` with ANSI 33/2, and session-name.ts renders `rs·`/`legacy·` with ANSI 33/2. They agree. If either side ever changes the word, nothing fails — the seam is a convention, not a contract. Worth one shared constant eventually; not worth blocking on.
- u1↔plan 126/127 (claude_settings.rs): additive. `ensure_claude_statusline` is a third peer of the existing `ensure_claude_inbound_accept` / `ensure_claude_session_start_hook`, wired into daemon boot at main.rs:1010 and into the same spine-emission and warning loops. It reuses `ensure_home`, `shell_command`, `find_top_level_value`, `insert_object_property`, `replace_range` unchanged. The statusline test asserts the SessionStart hook block survives the edit, which is the seam assertion I would have asked for.
- u2↔plan 128 (index.ts): the guide warned plan 128 also edits index.ts. This branch stayed inside the setSessionName call sites as instructed, and additionally renamed the retry-window `generation` parameter to `publicationGeneration` to make room for `daemonGeneration`. That rename is confined to one closure family and is the reason the two meanings do not collide — good call, and the second lander should keep it.
- Interface drift vs impl-guide.dd.json: none found. `publishSeatName(deps, self, generation: "rs"|"legacy")` matches the frozen interface exactly. `ensure_claude_statusline(homes, script) -> Vec<EnsureReport>` matches. The script exits 0 always and emits nothing for an unregistered pane — both verified by running it.

FLOWSPACE DOGFOOD (i1) — two frictions, reported as instructed:
1. `flowspace3 search "<q>" --mode semantic` — the form carried in the pij skill and in my own notes — is rejected by the installed flowspace3: `error: unexpected argument '--mode' found`. The usage line is now `flowspace3 search <QUERY>`. Anyone following the documented invocation hits an error before their first result.
2. Both meaning-shaped queries came back doc-dominated: "statusline resolves pane against rs before legacy" → 89 doc / 6 code, "publish omp session name with generation prefix" → 84 doc / 11 code. The top hit for both was plan prose describing the code, not the code. For a query phrased as a mechanism, the plan that promises the mechanism outranks the file that implements it — I found neither claude-statusline-pij.sh nor session-name.ts through search and reached both by reading the diff.

value.finding:
CLAIM (plan.dd.md AC1, G1): "dual-present panes show the rs id with a yellow rs tag" / "resolve the pane against rs FIRST ... fall back to legacy only when rs has no row".

DEFECT: the script calls `pij-rs --json whoami --pane "$TMUX_PANE"` while inheriting the Claude process's environment. When that environment exports a PIJ_SESSION_ID that rs does not agree is the owner of the pane, rs does not answer with the pane's row — it REFUSES, by design:

  {"ok":false,"command":"pij whoami","v":1,"meta":"the caller claims to be `pij-quarrelsome-caribou` but pane `%3060` belongs to `pij-relative-cheetah` — refusing rather than answering for either. An asserted id never outranks an observable one.","error":"refused"}   (exit 2)

The refusal body contains no `"id":"`, so the `case "$RS_OUTPUT" in *'"id":"'*` guard at :79-84 does not match, PIJID stays empty, and control falls to the legacy branch at :89. The pane then renders the LEGACY id under a dim `legacy` tag — the precise outcome AC1 exists to prevent, and it is not even a degraded-but-honest outcome: it asserts "legacy" about a pane that rs owns.

The population is not incidental. The contradiction arises exactly when a pane's exported id and its rs id differ, which is the definition of the mapped pairs named in the plan's own summary ("20 seats + 4 primes have both ids; map in briefs/seat-id-map-2026-09-02.md"). AC1's target population and the failing population are the same set.

PROOF — one pane, one script, one input, one variable. Pane %3060 is genuinely dual-present: `pij state pij-quarrelsome-caribou` reports pid 87487 alive, and `pij-rs whoami --pane %3060` reports pid 87487 under id pij-relative-cheetah.

  A) env PIJ_SESSION_ID=pij-quarrelsome-caribou TMUX_PANE=%3060 sh harness/scripts/claude-statusline-pij.sh
     -> ...ESC[2mlegacyESC[0m ESC[34m⛓ pij-quarrelsome-caribouESC[0m ...
  B) env -u PIJ_SESSION_ID  TMUX_PANE=%3060 sh harness/scripts/claude-statusline-pij.sh
     -> ...ESC[33mrsESC[0m ESC[34m⛓ pij-relative-cheetahESC[0m ...

The only difference between A and B is the inherited variable. A is what a real Claude statusline process gets; B is what the author's harness got.

WHY THE RECEIPTS DID NOT CATCH IT — and this is the more useful half. The AC1 fixture run (%2912) used a temp-PATH fake rs that returns a success row unconditionally, so it cannot express a refusal. The AC1 production capture on %2081 was taken by invoking the script with `--pane %2081` from a shell that was not that pane's Claude process, so it did not inherit that pane's PIJ_SESSION_ID. Both observations are true; neither observes the production path. The captured statusline JSON was real, which makes the setup feel like a live test — but the env, not the stdin, is what decides this.

SMALLEST FIX — one word at harness/scripts/claude-statusline-pij.sh:78:
  RS_OUTPUT=$(env -u PIJ_SESSION_ID "$PIJ_RS_BIN" --json whoami --pane "$TMUX_PANE" 2>/dev/null)
`--pane` already supplies the observable, so the asserted id is not merely unnecessary here, it is the only thing that can make the observable unreachable. Verified: this is exactly the difference between run A and run B above.

Do not fix it only in the script. `--pane` is an explicit "answer for THIS pane" gesture; a caller that names a pane has stopped claiming to be anyone. Prime may want rs to ignore PIJ_SESSION_ID whenever `--pane` is given, which would fix every future caller instead of this one — that is a seam decision above my fence, so I name it rather than take it.
value.receipt: live A/B on pane %3060 (dual-present, pid 87487 in both stores) with the branch script and identical stdin; `pij-rs --json whoami --pane %3060` run under three env states (contradicting id -> refused/exit 2, unset -> ok, matching -> ok); script :73-93 read in full; claude_settings.rs:1586-1596 fake read

value.finding:
CLAIM (plan.dd.md AC4): "statusline script wall time with rs answering ≤ 50ms over 10 runs (hyperfine or time loop), pasted".

DEFECT: the delivered evidence does not meet the promise as the plan states it, and the plan text was never amended to the bar that was actually ruled. assets/live-statusline.md records "Prime ruled the target as median of 10 warm runs ≤100 ms" with a median of 92.10ms. plan.dd.md still says 50ms. Whoever reads the plan record next — including the ship gate — reads a promise that the receipt beside it does not keep, and has to reconstruct from prose that a different bar was substituted.

PROOF — my own 10 warm runs on the rs path, same script, captured real-shape JSON, host load 67.22 recorded:
  54.0, 60.6, 60.8, 60.9, 61.8, 74.2, 78.9, 85.5, 85.5, 90.4 ms   median 67.98 ms
(my loop adds one `sh -c` and one `printf` per iteration, so the true figure is somewhat lower.) I reproduce the author's shape: comfortably inside 100ms, not inside 50ms. I have no quarrel with 100ms as a bar — the statusline is not on a 300ms critical path in any way that 68ms threatens, and the 28× improvement over the tsx path is real and large. The finding is that the plan and its receipt state different bars.

SMALLEST FIX: amend AC4's text in plan.dd.json to the ruled ≤100ms and rebuild, so the ruling replaces the superseded number rather than sitting beside it in a different file. Two authoritative bars in two documents is how the next reader picks the wrong one.
value.receipt: own 10-run warm timing loop on the rs path, raw values and host load 67.22 recorded; plan.dd.md AC4 text read; assets/live-statusline.md AC4 section read

value.finding:
CLAIM (impl-guide u1 test_strategy): "script tested with a fake pij-rs on PATH returning a row / no row".

DEFECT: the fake is `#!/bin/sh; printf '{"ok":true,"data":{"id":"pij-rs-seat"}}'` — it ignores `--pane`, ignores the environment, and has exactly two behaviours: unconditional success, or (for the miss half) `exit 1` with no output. Production rs has a third behaviour that this fake cannot express: answer with a row, OR refuse because the caller's asserted id contradicts the pane. The test is green and will stay green through #findings/f1, because the world it arranges is one where the asserted id never matters. That is why f1 shipped past a test written specifically to prove rs-first resolution.

Secondary, same root: the miss is modelled as `exit 1` with empty stdout, whereas real rs misses and refusals exit 2 WITH a JSON body. The script's `case` guard happens to handle both identically, so this is not itself a defect — but it means the test has never seen the actual bytes the script parses in the failure path, and a future parser change (say, to `grep -o` or `jq`) could pass this test while breaking on real output.

PROOF: crates/harnesses/src/claude_settings.rs:1586-1596 (fake bodies) and :1618-1622 (the `.env(...)` list — TMUX_PANE and LEGACY_MARKER are set; PIJ_SESSION_ID never is). Test read in full; `cargo test -p pij-harnesses statusline_` watched, 4 passed.

SMALLEST FIX: make the fake read its arguments and its environment — refuse with the real refusal shape when `$PIJ_SESSION_ID` is set and differs from the row it would return, answer otherwise — then add one case that sets `PIJ_SESSION_ID=pij-other-seat` and asserts the yellow `rs` tag with the rs id. Written against today's script that case fails; against the f1 fix it passes. That is the witness the current test does not have.
value.receipt: statusline_script_prefers_rs_and_falls_back_to_legacy read in full (:1576-1663); `cargo test -p pij-harnesses statusline_` watched, 4 passed

value.finding:
CLAIM (impl-guide u2, and the packet's third least-confident area): rs/legacy generation propagates through initial publication AND turn_start reassertion.

DEFECT: the code is correct — index.ts:552-556 passes `publication.daemonGeneration` into the reassertion call, and I read it rather than inferring it. But the test that covers that path asserts only `expect(sessionNames).toHaveLength(2)`. It counts publications; it never looks at what was published. Delete the `publication.daemonGeneration` argument and the reassertion would republish a bare id with no generation prefix, and index.test.ts:276-291 would still pass. The startup path is properly witnessed on both generations (index.test.ts:234-260 asserts `/^rs·.../` and `/^legacy·.../` plus both status-row spellings); the reassertion path — the half the packet flagged as least-confident — is the one with no witness.

PROOF: index.test.ts:276-291 read in full; grep for the generation spellings across both test files returns hits only in the startup cases and session-name.test.ts:197. 17/17 and 8/8 watched green, which is exactly the point: green is not evidence for a claim nobody asserted.

SMALLEST FIX: at index.test.ts:286, add `expect(sessionNames.at(-1)).toMatch(/^rs·pij-/)`. One line, and it converts a passing count into a witness for the seam the packet was worried about.
value.receipt: index.ts:544-560 and index.test.ts:276-291 read in full; grep for `rs·`/`legacy·`/ANSI spellings across both test files; vitest watched, 17/17 and 8/8

value.finding: NOTE FOR PRIME, not a finding against this plan — `backup_statusline_script` returns Ok(()) and takes no backup in three cases it cannot distinguish from success: a `~/`-prefixed command when `home.parent()` is not the real $HOME (a CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR outside the home directory), a relative command, and a command with arguments or an interpreter prefix (`sh ~/foo.sh`). The consequence is bounded — the prior script file is never deleted, only dereferenced, so nothing is lost, and I confirmed the mechanism works for both forms that occur in practice: `~/.claude/statusline-context.sh` and `/Users/jordanknight/.claude/statusline-context.sh` both produced real backups on the operator's disk today. I raise it because the incident recorded in the receipts was recovered FROM these backups, which makes silent non-backup a worse failure here than its bounded blast radius suggests. A one-line `error:` on the report when the previous command could not be resolved to a file would make the silence audible without changing behaviour.
value.receipt: backup_statusline_script :185-215 read; `ls ~/.claude | grep -i statusline` shows statusline-context.sh.bak-1788315355478 (from the tilde form) and .bak-1788316617931 (from the absolute form); `jq .statusLine.command` across four of today's settings backups shows both command spellings occurred

value.rationale: Blocking. AC1 is false for the mapped-pair population it was written for, reproduced live on a real dual-present pane with a one-variable A/B. The fix is one `env -u` at :78; the seam question of whether rs should ignore an asserted id when `--pane` is given is prime's, and I name it rather than decide it.

Not blocking on performance grounds — 68ms is fine and the 28x improvement is real. Blocking on record integrity: plan.dd.md promises 50ms, the receipt delivers 92ms against a separately-ruled 100ms bar, and the two live in different files. Amend the AC text so the ruling replaces the superseded number instead of sitting beside it.

This is the reason f1 shipped green. The fake rs cannot express a refusal, so the test that exists to prove rs-first resolution is structurally incapable of failing on the way rs-first resolution actually breaks. Fixing f1 without fixing this leaves the next regression equally invisible.
One line. The code is right today; the assertion is what stops it being refactored away, and the reassertion path is precisely the seam the packet named as least-confident.

Recorded for prime, outside this plan's scope per w2. The mechanism demonstrably works for both command spellings that occur in practice; the concern is that it fails silently for the ones that do not.
